title: Supply chain disruption on auto manufacturer stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study with cross-sectional heterogeneity
- Why: The semiconductor shortage announcement is a plausibly exogenous, time-localized information shock. Event studies isolate the stock-price response to such shocks by comparing realized returns to model-implied normal returns over a short window. Cross-sectional regressions on chip dependency test whether exposure explains variation in firms’ cumulative abnormal returns (CARs).
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding firm-specific news systematically coinciding with the announcement across the sample.
  - The market model is correctly specified over the short horizon; betas are stable from the estimation window to the event window.
  - The event is not anticipated (limited pre-trend in [-1, -1] or [-2, -1]).
  - For the cross-section, chip dependency is predetermined and uncorrelated with omitted determinants of surprise at the announcement (beyond common market factors), so it captures heterogeneity in exposure rather than correlated confounders.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load libraries
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(dplyr)
  library(sandwich)
  library(lmtest)
  library(broom)
})

# Path to data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s16_data.csv"

# Read data
dt <- fread(path)

# Basic checks
req_cols <- c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret")
stopifnot(all(req_cols %in% names(dt)))

# Try to locate a chip dependency variable (case-insensitive search)
chip_candidates <- names(dt)[grepl("chip", names(dt), ignore.case = TRUE)]
if (length(chip_candidates) == 0) {
  stop("No chip dependency variable found. Expected a column containing 'chip' (e.g., 'chip_dep').")
}
# Prefer a canonical name if present
preferred <- c("chip_dep","chip_dependency","chip_intensity","chip_exposure")
chip_var <- intersect(preferred, chip_candidates)
chip_var <- if (length(chip_var) > 0) chip_var[1] else chip_candidates[1]

# Ensure types
dt[, event_day := as.integer(event_day)]
dt <- dt[!is.na(ret) & !is.na(mkt_ret)]

# Estimation window and event windows
est_win <- c(-10, -2)
event_win_main <- c(0, 5)
event_win_alt1 <- c(0, 2)
event_win_alt2 <- c(0, 3)
event_win_alt3 <- c(-1, 1)

# Helper: estimate per-stock market model on [-10,-2] via OLS
est_dt <- dt[event_day >= est_win[1] & event_day <= est_win[2]]
# Require at least 5 observations in estimation window to estimate model
min_est_n <- 5

coefs <- est_dt[ , {
  if (.N < min_est_n) {
    list(alpha = NA_real_, beta_hat = NA_real_, n = .N)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit) || anyNA(coef(fit))) {
      list(alpha = NA_real_, beta_hat = NA_real_, n = .N)
    } else {
      cf <- coef(fit)
      list(alpha = unname(cf[1]), beta_hat = unname(cf[2]), n = .N)
    }
  }
}, by = stock_id]

coefs <- coefs[!is.na(alpha) & !is.na(beta_hat)]

# Merge coefficients back, compute abnormal returns (OLS version)
dt_ols <- merge(dt, coefs, by = "stock_id", all.x = FALSE)
dt_ols[, ar_ols := ret - (alpha + beta_hat * mkt_ret)]

# Alternative abnormal returns: market-adjusted (ret - mkt_ret)
dt_ols[, ar_mktadj := ret - mkt_ret]

# Alternative: Use provided beta (if present) with alpha estimated using that beta on est window
use_beta_provided <- "beta" %in% names(dt_ols)
if (use_beta_provided) {
  # Estimate alpha with provided beta: alpha_i = mean(ret - beta_i * mkt_ret) over est window
  alpha_fix <- est_dt[, .(alpha_fix = mean(ret - first(beta) * mkt_ret, na.rm = TRUE)), by = stock_id]
  dt_ols <- merge(dt_ols, alpha_fix, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
  dt_ols[, ar_fixbeta := ret - (alpha_fix + beta * mkt_ret)]
}

# Build stock-level chip dependency measure (take first non-missing)
chip_by_stock <- dt_ols[ , {
  v <- get(chip_var)
  list(chip = v[which(!is.na(v))[1]])
}, by = stock_id]

# Function to compute CARs and summarize
compute_car_summary <- function(data, ar_col, win, min_days = 5) {
  ev <- data[event_day >= win[1] & event_day <= win[2]]
  car <- ev[ , .(
    CAR = sum(get(ar_col), na.rm = FALSE),
    days = sum(!is.na(get(ar_col)))
  ), by = stock_id]
  # Require at least min_days observed days in event window for inclusion
  car <- car[days >= min_days]
  N <- nrow(car)
  if (N < 5) {
    return(list(N = N, meanCAR = NA_real_, t = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, car_df = car))
  }
  m <- mean(car$CAR)
  s <- sd(car$CAR)
  tstat <- m / (s / sqrt(N))
  pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = N - 1)
  list(N = N, meanCAR = m, t = tstat, p = pval, car_df = car)
}

# Main CAR summary: OLS market model, [0,5], require >=5 of 6 days
main_sum <- compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_ols", event_win_main, min_days = 5)

# Robustness: alternative event windows (OLS market model)
alt1_sum <- compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_ols", event_win_alt1, min_days = 3)
alt2_sum <- compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_ols", event_win_alt2, min_days = 4)
alt3_sum <- compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_ols", event_win_alt3, min_days = 3)

# Robustness: alternative abnormal return models on [0,5]
mktadj_sum <- compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_mktadj", event_win_main, min_days = 5)
fixbeta_sum <- if (use_beta_provided) compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_fixbeta", event_win_main, min_days = 5) else NULL

# Cross-sectional regression: CAR on chip dependency (main window, OLS ARs)
car_cs <- merge(main_sum$car_df[, .(stock_id, CAR_ols = CAR)],
                chip_by_stock, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
car_cs <- car_cs[!is.na(chip)]

# Also bring along estimated beta_hat and provided beta (if available) for robustness
betas_est <- unique(dt_ols[, .(stock_id, beta_hat = beta_hat)])
car_cs <- merge(car_cs, betas_est, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
if (use_beta_provided) {
  beta_prov <- unique(dt_ols[, .(stock_id, beta_prov = beta)])
  car_cs <- merge(car_cs, beta_prov, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
}

# Main cross-sectional regression: CAR_ols ~ chip
fit_cs <- lm(CAR_ols ~ chip, data = car_cs)
fit_cs_rob <- coeftest(fit_cs, vcov = vcovHC(fit_cs, type = "HC1"))

# Robust CS: add beta_hat control
fit_cs_b <- lm(CAR_ols ~ chip + beta_hat, data = car_cs)
fit_cs_b_rob <- coeftest(fit_cs_b, vcov = vcovHC(fit_cs_b, type = "HC1"))

# If provided beta exists, another robustness with beta_prov
if (use_beta_provided) {
  fit_cs_bp <- lm(CAR_ols ~ chip + beta_prov, data = car_cs)
  fit_cs_bp_rob <- coeftest(fit_cs_bp, vcov = vcovHC(fit_cs_bp, type = "HC1"))
}

# Summaries and clear numerical outputs
to_pct <- function(x) 100 * x

cat("Event Study Results (Market Model OLS on [-10,-2], Event Window [0,5])\n")
cat(sprintf("Stocks used (N): %d\n", main_sum$N))
cat(sprintf("Average CAR [0,5]: %.3f%%\n", to_pct(main_sum$meanCAR)))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic: %.2f, p-value: %.4f\n\n", main_sum$t, main_sum$p))

cat("Cross-Sectional Regression: CAR_ols ~ chip\n")
gamma1 <- fit_cs_rob["chip", "Estimate"]
tchip  <- fit_cs_rob["chip", "t value"]
pchip  <- fit_cs_rob["chip", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Coefficient on chip: %.3f (CAR per 1-unit chip), t=%.2f, p=%.4f\n", gamma1, tchip, pchip))
# Economic magnitude: per 1 SD in chip
sd_chip <- sd(car_cs$chip, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Implied effect per 1 SD increase in chip (SD=%.3f): %.3f%% CAR\n\n", sd_chip, to_pct(gamma1 * sd_chip)))

cat("Robustness: Add estimated beta control (CAR_ols ~ chip + beta_hat)\n")
gamma1_b <- fit_cs_b_rob["chip", "Estimate"]; tchip_b <- fit_cs_b_rob["chip", "t value"]; pchip_b <- fit_cs_b_rob["chip", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Coefficient on chip: %.3f, t=%.2f, p=%.4f\n\n", gamma1_b, tchip_b, pchip_b))

if (use_beta_provided) {
  cat("Robustness: Add provided beta control (CAR_ols ~ chip + beta_prov)\n")
  gamma1_bp <- fit_cs_bp_rob["chip", "Estimate"]; tchip_bp <- fit_cs_bp_rob["chip", "t value"]; pchip_bp <- fit_cs_bp_rob["chip", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  cat(sprintf("Coefficient on chip: %.3f, t=%.2f, p=%.4f\n\n", gamma1_bp, tchip_bp, pchip_bp))
}

cat("Robustness: Alternative Event Windows (OLS market model)\n")
cat(sprintf("[0,2] Avg CAR: %.3f%% (N=%d)\n", to_pct(alt1_sum$meanCAR), alt1_sum$N))
cat(sprintf("[0,3] Avg CAR: %.3f%% (N=%d)\n", to_pct(alt2_sum$meanCAR), alt2_sum$N))
cat(sprintf("[-1,1] Avg CAR: %.3f%% (N=%d)\n\n", to_pct(alt3_sum$meanCAR), alt3_sum$N))

cat("Robustness: Alternative Abnormal Return Models on [0,5]\n")
cat(sprintf("Market-adjusted (ret - mkt_ret) Avg CAR: %.3f%% (N=%d)\n", to_pct(mktadj_sum$meanCAR), mktadj_sum$N))
if (!is.null(fixbeta_sum)) {
  cat(sprintf("Provided beta with re-estimated alpha Avg CAR: %.3f%% (N=%d)\n", to_pct(fixbeta_sum$meanCAR), fixbeta_sum$N))
}

# Also print simple pre-trend diagnostic (mean AR on [-2,-1])
pre_sum <- compute_car_summary(dt_ols, "ar_ols", c(-2, -1), min_days = 2)
cat(sprintf("\nPre-trend check [-2,-1] Avg CAR: %.3f%% (t=%.2f, p=%.4f, N=%d)\n",
            to_pct(pre_sum$meanCAR), pre_sum$t, pre_sum$p, pre_sum$N))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Time-series CAR: Negative average CAR over [0,5], reflecting the adverse cash-flow and production implications of a semiconductor shortage for auto manufacturers. Magnitude around −1% to −2.5% over six trading days is plausible for a major surprise.
- Cross-sectional heterogeneity: A more negative CAR for firms with higher chip dependency. The coefficient on chip dependency should be negative. Economic size: a 1 standard deviation increase in chip dependency could correspond to roughly −0.5% to −1.0% additional CAR.
- Robustness: The negative effect should persist across alternative event windows and abnormal-return models, with minimal pre-trend in [-2,−1].

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study + cross-sectional CAR regression on firm-level exposure variable
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Auto stocks decline; higher chip-dependency → larger CAR loss
